localLife.nature: Before it was 1.8 million people and a quarter-million acres of postwar tract homes, the Valley was citrus groves and walnut orchards — the same flat basin that made it good farmland now traps summer heat across the entire floor with nothing but freeways and surface streets to break it up.
localLife.community: Millions of people across dozens of distinct neighborhoods, all connected by the same grid of boulevards and freeways, all dependent on a car to get almost anywhere, and all living under the same basin-wide heat that doesn't care which specific neighborhood you're in.
localLife.howWeHelp: We size systems for the reality of basin-wide heat — a valley floor that runs hotter than the surrounding hills and coast by design, not by neighborhood — and we dispatch across the full Valley without treating any part of it as an afterthought.

seasonalNotes.focus: The valley floor as a whole runs 10-15 degrees hotter than the LA basin's coastal side on a typical summer day — a basin-wide heat-island effect that has nothing to do with which specific neighborhood a home sits in.
Santa Ana wind events sweep the length of the Valley from the northwest passes to the east — filtration and duct-sealing checks matter basin-wide before wind season, not just in one corner of it.
